properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/30/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8167177
Permit API: 015-20621
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Herrick Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/30/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Greenzweig GU-D (Reeve-Sutton) well pad located in Herrick Township, Bradford County on 11/30/2023 at 1030 hours. The weather was 38 degrees with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the DEP by SWN. DEP Environmental Trainees, Erica Lutz and Evan Buck, accompanied me during the inspection.SWN reported to the DEP reporting hotline that at ~0300 hours on 11/30/2023 a release of >5 gallons of coolant (ethylene glycol) was spilled to the pad surface at their GU-D (Reeve-Sutton) site. Onsite today, SWN reported that repairs were made to the compressor unit's exhaust manifold after a small leak was noticed, which was all captured by the secondary containment skid. After repairs were complete, the reservoir was refilled with coolant and ended up overtopping the reservoir tank. The overtopping coolant was captured by the secondary containment skid but the skid ended up overtopping as well, causing the release to the pad surface. During this inspection, the majority of the impacted material had been collected but further recovery was underway. SWN reported that glycol test kits would be utilized to confirm that the entire portion of the release was recovered. See photos #1 and 2 for an overview of the release area. No evidence would suggest that any portion of the release was able to escape the gravel surface of the pad.Later in the day, SWN reported via email that the release was further calculated and reported a final release volume of 4-5 gallons of coolant was able to escape secondary containment. The final cleanup photos prior to backfilling are attached (photos #3 and 4) and were provided by the operator.Violations of the following are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against API #015-20621:SWMA 301CSL 402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56aWe departed the site at 1120 hours.

Comments: On 4/6/22 an incident inspection of the Pettit GH84 OG Well site was conducted in response to a report of spill received by the Department on 4/4/22. Initial details of the spill were reported by CNX at approximately 5:30pm on 4/4/22. The report stated that at approximately 3:30pm on 4/4/22 a leak was discovered around the valve of buried waterline at the GH84 well site. It was estimated that two barrels of brine were released. On 4/6/22 at approximately 8:45am, I called Kyle Borden of CNX to inquire about the spill. He stated that a leak was discovered in a buried three-inch polyline leading from the GH84 coalbed methane well to a tank battery. The leak was discovered by the lease operator during a routine inspection on 4/4/22. The well had previously been inspected on 3/30/22 and no leak was observed at that time. The lease operator observed an orange/red fluid saturating the ground behind the well pumpjack. The well was shut in upon discovery of the leak. Mr. Borden stated that excavation of the area began on 4/5/22. Due to overnight precipitation, the excavated area needed pumped the morning of 4/6/22. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI was contracted for remediation and Penn E&R was contracted for sampling. During the site inspection, the following was observed: -A crew was on-site excavating impacted substrate from the spill area (Photos #1-3 and #8). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the area that was actively being remediated. -BMPs were observed downslope of the disturbed area (Photos #5-6). -The area below the installed BMPs (Photo #7) did not exhibit elevated conductivity. -A well sign was posted at the pumpjack (Photo #9). Mr. Borden stated that after the initial remediation efforts, following the overnight precipitation, elevated conductivity was observed in the area that had been excavated. Upon further remediation of the area, Mr. Borden estimated that five barrels of brine were released. CNX plans to continue excavation of impacted material until elevated conductivity is no longer detected. An additional roll-off container was in route to the site at the time of the inspection. Mr. Borden stated that four roll-off boxes had already been filled and removed from the site. CNX is following Act 2 protocol for the spill. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, and 78.54 are being issued for the release.

Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. On 3/27/23, an administrative order was issued due to a lack of remedial action from Stonehaven Energy. This order was delivered in person by Bureau of Investigations staff on 3/28/2023. As per this administrative order, a written remediation plan was to be submitted to the Department by 5/26/23, and a final remediation report is to be submitted by 12/31/23. No Remediation Schedule has been received, and a new violation has been issued for failure to comply with the terms of the issued court order.During an inspection of the site on 4/20/23, it was noted that a partial soil excavation had occurred. At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any further excavation has occurred since that date. The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/7/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655977), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

Violation ID: 855649

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-07-15
Comments: On July 15, 2019, Department representative Brad Kline and Jared Jacobini conducted an investigation of a reported spill from production fluid tank secondary containment. The Department met with Nathan Harris from Pennsylvania General Energy and discussed how the hole occurred. PGE estimated about 2-3 barrels were spilled from the containment of the production fluid tanks secondary containment. At the time of inspection, the impacted soil had been excavated below 2,500 uS/cm. The area impacted was about 20' x 15' and about 5 inches of soil in the area has been removed. Moody and Associates were delineating the area and collecting soil samples. The impacted area was limited to the pad surface. The release of production fluid outside of secondary containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), 78a.57(a), and Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act. 78a.64(a)(g) states that stormwater that comes into contact with a regulated substances stored within the secondary containment shall be managed as residual waste. Thus, due to the presence of produced water mixed with stormwater and the reported volume of the release,the remediation under Act 2 is required under 78a.66(c).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/29/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2025
Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 8242709
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2025
Comments: On July 29, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQTs Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 7/28/2025 at 2:54 pm.The spill report stated that at 2:06 pm on 7/28/2025, over 5 gallons of production fluids were found on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site after removing secondary containment. Accompanying during today's inspection is EQTs representative Kyle Borden.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had different Operator information on it than the Act 9 sign. The DEP recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. At the time of this inspection, drill outs were recently completed on the 6U and containment was removed from the well pad the day prior. Mr. Borden stated that the secondary containment in the release area was packed with tanks and large equipment, therefore despite routine inspections of the containment, only the edges of the containment could be inspected, and no holes or tears were observed. However, upon removal of the containment, staining and small puddles were observed on the gravel pad in an approximately 115 ft x 60 ft area. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to wellheads covered by boxes. The pea gravel in this area was observed to be wet with sections that appeared to be darker in color than other areas. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI and Moody were arriving on site to remediate the release and that they estimate remediation to be completed within the day. EQT representative Schuyler Brounce mentioned in his email (documented in IR 4024285), that following his review of the incident, he estimates the release to be over 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Borden stated once all contaminated gravel has been removed, an updated quantity will be provided to the DEP.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected soil readings of 1.835 mS, 3.22 mS, 3.35 mS and 2.08 mS in the incident area closest to the wellheads, as well as 2.56 mS between two wellheads and a fluid reading of Over Range in fluid observed to be pooled in secondary containment adjacent to the release area. These conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil reading of 0.1457 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign.At the time of this inspection, the DEP requested secondary containment logs for the Porter well pad and Mr. Borden stated they would be provided to the Department electronically. The DEP is also requesting an electronic copy of the Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals stored/utilized within and near the secondary containment that was observed to have the release underneath by COB 8/5/2025.The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the over 1 barrel release of production fluids on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Violation ID: 8223942
Permit API: 003-22235
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/05/2025
Comments: On March 5, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Oliver East well pad in Forward Township, Allegheny County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3913651. IR 3913651 was conducted in response to the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure which reportedly released 5-10 gallons of produced water to the surface of the well pad. Notice of Termination request was approved by the Department for this site on November 10, 2022.The following was observed:The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 22). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 1). Sediment from the access road appears to threaten a stormwater drain along Williamsport Road (see photo 23). Although no sediment was observed inside this stormwater drain at the time of inspection, a layer of sediment was observed on debris that had accumulated on top of the storm drain grate.The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 3). Well 4H is equipped with a well tag with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be equipped for production (see photos 5 and 6). There are fourteen additional well heads onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 4). An additional storage tank placed within secondary containment was observed onsite (see photo 7). This secondary containment appears to be holding a significant amount of rainwater at the time of inspection. Old GPU units are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. New GPU units onsite are equipped with secondary containment (see photo 8).A reported absorbent material has been applied to the majority of the area impacted by the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure (see photos 10-12). The conductivity of the soil underneath this reported absorbent material remains significantly higher than the surrounding soil (see photos 13-20). The soil conductivity meter utilized for this inspection was calibrated immediately prior to conducting this inspection. Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and therefore remediation appears to be incomplete. Because it appears that not all impacted material has been removed and greater than 15 days has passed since the 1/29/2025 dumpline failure occurred, violations shall be issued in this inspection report.The Department continues to recommend that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to function as intended in the event of a release. The Department also recommends that the operator take immediate measures to address and prevent potential pollution due to sediment discharge from the access road to the Waters of the Commonwealth.

Comments: On August 2, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report. The spill was called in to the Department today at 9:54 AM by the Operator, who described a 25-26 barrel release of crude oil that was found by a well tender at 8:40 AM. Operator will be utilizing Act 2 standards for clean up.The Department arrived on site at approximately 1:15 PM and spoke with Paul Steiner of Diversified. According to Steiner, a well tender discovered the release at approximately 8:40 AM from a crack (Photo 3) in the storage/production tank on site. Steiner approximated the total release to be 26 barrels based on the amount of crude oil in the production tank last week (approximately 4 feet) and the amount of crude oil still in the tank at discovery, which is an approximate 22 inches.The release migrated towards and past the production equipment (Photo 4) and down an embankment, where it reportedly stopped at a berm (Photo 8) according to Steiner. Steiner is using a PID meter to detect the extent of the oil's migration. During the on site inspection, Diversified was excavating impacted material at the berm and moving it upslope so that they can place it into a Spartan dump truck to have it transported for disposal. Steiner says one truck load will be transported tonight, excavation will stop, then another Spartan truck will arrive tomorrow morning, excavation will resume, and remaining impacted material will be taken off site before Moody arrives in the afternoon to confirm complete site clean up. Oil absorbent booms will be placed around and downslope of the impacted material overnight tonight to prevent further migration between truck loads, according to Steiner.Following the inspection, Steiner and myself spoke with DCNR Park Manager Kris Baker of Keystone State Park at the park office to notify the park of the release.Violations issued for spill. The Department requests disposal documents when made available.

Inspection Date: 9/21/2026
Comments: On September 21, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response site inspection at the EQT ARO LLC COP Tract 027B Pad B. EQT reported to the DEP spill hotline that a water truck hauling produced fluid spilled approximately 100 gallons of produced fluid from a faulty sight glass on the water truck onto the access road of the well pad at 0800. Upon arriving onsite, EQT had delineated the spill on the access road and had that area blocked off from traffic. EQT said that Penn E and R was responding to assist with the investigation and collect confirmatory samples for the ACT 2 process. EQT was investigating how much of the produce fluid had spilled off the road edge. Approximately three areas along the road edge were found to have elevated soil conductivity. One of the areas found was a culvert with produced fluid caught in the outfall. The soil conductivity of the impacted area ranged from 200 uS/cm to over 4,000 uS/cm, which is the upper limit of the DEP soil conductivity meter. The delineated area of impact was approximately 10 feet by 415 feet measure by Penn E and R. While onsite, equipment was delivered to begin the excavation of the impacted area. EQT's contractor began removing the impacted soil from the access road. The contractor scraped the road surface and excavated approximately 4-6 inches of soil off the road edge to removed the impacted soil. Approximately 100 feet of the spill area had been excavated prior to DEP leaving the site. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 401, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted. EQT plans to remediate the spill through the ACT 2 process.
